items.content_html:
snouty acts as a Docker credential helper for the Antithesis tenant registry when it is started as docker-credential-snouty, the name Docker and Podman run for a credHelpers entry. Upstream's shell installer and their own package.nix create that name as a symlink to snouty, and this does the same.

The package also failed to build on master. #537108 made cargoSetupHook set LIBSQLITE3_SYS_USE_PKG_CONFIG for every Rust build, so libsqlite3-sys now links the system sqlite instead of its bundled copy, and linking failed with cannot find -lsqlite3. The 0.9.1 bump was branched before that change landed. The first commit adds sqlite to buildInputs, and drops openssl, which snouty no longer depends on. snouty uses sqlite only for the FTS5 index behind snouty docs.

The last commit updates snouty from 0.9.1 to 0.10.0 (changelog). snouty 0.10.0 depends on aws-lc-sys, and cargoSetupHook sets AWS_LC_SYS_USE_SYSTEM, so the commit adds aws-lc to buildInputs.

Each commit builds on x86_64-linux with all tests passing (1047 tests on 0.10.0). docker-credential-snouty get answers the helper protocol, and snouty docs search works against the live docs database.

This change was written with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.2), and each commit carries an Assisted-by: trailer.

items.content_html:
Closes #22953

On NixOS, containers always ran unconfined even with security.apparmor.enable = true, and docker run --security-opt apparmor=<nonexistent> was silently accepted.

Root cause

dockerd only sets process.apparmorProfile in the OCI spec if containerd's apparmor.HostSupports() returns true. That function requires /sbin/apparmor_parser to exist. NixOS has no /sbin, so it was always false and runc never received a profile (process.apparmorProfile was null in the container's config.json).

Changes

When security.apparmor.enable is set:

  • add apparmor-parser to the docker service path (dockerd execs it to load its generated docker-default)
  • symlink /sbin/apparmor_parser via systemd.tmpfiles
  • provide /etc/apparmor.d/tunables/global (plus apparmor-profiles in the include path). moby only includes <tunables/global> in the generated profile if that file exists literally; otherwise the profile fails to load with Failed to find declaration for: @{HOMEDIRS}.

Adds a NixOS test node asserting a container reports docker-default (enforce).

Testing

  • nixosTests.docker passes on x86_64-linux (the new subtest fails without the tunables/global part, as found while iterating).
  • Also running on a real system (Docker 29.9.2, runc 1.5.2, apparmor 4.1.7): three containers confined as docker-default (enforce) with dockerd generating the profile itself, without a hand-written security.apparmor.policies.docker-default.

AI disclosure

The investigation and the patch were done with Claude Code (Claude Sonnet 5.5). I reviewed the diff, ran the NixOS test and verified the behaviour on my own machine.

Things done

  • Fits CONTRIBUTING.md
  • Follows the automation/AI policy (disclosure above)
  • Built on platform:
    • x86_64-linux
  • Tested, as applicable:
    • NixOS tests in nixos/tests

Adds an extraCliPlugins option to the package definition to include
additional arbitrary docker plugins. This allows injecting plugins that
aren't included by default in the package definition to be usable by the
CLI without changing the full package definition which allows overrides
to include extra packages that aren't included in nixpkgs.

It promotes component packages used to build Docker to top-level parameters, which allows overrides of the package.

If done well, only the syntax of the file should change to allow users to override Docker, but no packages should rebuild.

items.content_html:
Description of changes

nix-prefetch-docker failed to run when the target Docker image didn't exist for the host platform, regardless of the target platform specified for the image.

$ nix-prefetch-docker --json pihole/pihole 2023.02.1
FATA[0001] Error parsing manifest for image: choosing image instance: no image found in manifest list for architecture amd64, variant "", OS darwin

The failure occurred because some calls to the skopeo CLI didn't specify the target OS and architecture. This change fixes the problem by wrapping every call to skopeo.
